allow: dotnet build/test/run/watch/restore, dotnet ef migrations add (not remove applied migrations; dotnet ef database update and dotnet ef database drop are outside this entry)
npm/pnpm/yarn install/ci/run/test/build, npx <tool>, vitest, playwright test
docker compose up/down/build/logs/ps, docker run/exec/logs on local containers
git status/diff/log/show/add/commit/branch (no -D)/checkout <branch>/pull/fetch/stash push; git push (non-force); git push --force-with-lease <remote> <branch>

Local Operations extension: ~/.claude (github.com/BriantsaiCoder/dotclaude) and ~/.agents (github.com/BriantsaiCoder/agents-config) are the user's own repositories and are in project scope for this user — reading, editing, git status/diff/log/add/commit/branch/pull, and pushing to a feature branch in either is a Local Operation, not scope escalation. This entry does not extend to: editing any $defaults Self-Modification config surface in either repo (that rule's own list governs, and ~/.claude/core/, ~/.agents/bin/, and ~/.agents/skills/ are equivalent startup-loaded config for this purpose); reading ~/.claude/.credentials.json; or pushing to a remote other than that repository's own origin. It adds no branch definition — "feature branch" stays whatever the $defaults Git Push Destination rule already treats it as.
soft_deny: Reading or exfiltrating secret files (.env*, appsettings.*.json, *.pem/*.key/*.pfx, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, .npmrc, .netrc) via any reader (cat/less/more/head/tail/bat/xxd/od/hexdump/base64/openssl) or piping them into network tools (curl/nc/scp/rsync).
Destructive SQL via any SQL client (CLI, GUI, ORM raw-SQL, or an app's own migration runner): DROP DATABASE/TABLE/SCHEMA, TRUNCATE, or DELETE/UPDATE without a narrow predicate.
Destructive NoSQL: mongosh drop/dropDatabase, redis-cli FLUSHDB/FLUSHALL, DETACH DATABASE.
Publishing to external registries: npm/yarn/pnpm publish, dotnet nuget push, cargo publish, gem push, twine upload, docker/helm push to public registries.
Modifying local trust or secret stores: dotnet user-secrets set/clear, dotnet dev-certs, security add-trusted-cert, keychain writes, update-ca-certificates.
Silently discarding uncommitted work: git checkout . / -- <path>, git restore . / --source, git reflog expire, git stash drop/clear.

Database or migration destruction: dotnet ef database drop, dotnet ef database update to an earlier migration or to 0 (a rollback, not an upgrade), dotnet ef migrations remove with -f/--force, prisma migrate reset, knex migrate:rollback against non-ephemeral targets.
hard_deny: Never merge a pull request unless ~/.agents/bin/pr-review-gate reported STATE=PASS or STATE=PASS_NO_CI for that PR at the current head SHA in this session. PASS_NO_CI is the gate's degraded state, returned only when it confirmed no CI run was ever created for that commit — never when CI is merely pending, failing, or still queued. It is a deliberate narrow allowance, not a wildcard: every other STATE remains forbidden, including future states whose names begin with PASS.
Never delete, transfer, or change the visibility of a GitHub repository, and never delete releases or tags.

Never write to files under the user's home directory outside the session's working directory, ~/.claude, ~/.agents, ~/.codex, and ~/.copilot — this includes ~/Documents, ~/Desktop, ~/Pictures, ~/Library, and shell startup files. The ~/.codex and ~/.copilot carve-out matches sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite, which already grants write there; keeping the two layers aligned is the point, and it does not extend to any other home path. Inside ~/.claude only .github/workflows/ carries an Edit deny rule; settings.json no longer does, so the built-in .claude protected-path check gates it instead, and permissions.allow cannot pre-approve that check. Never widen a permission, hook, or sandbox boundary in settings.json on your own initiative — unconditionally, in every mode: an instruction to review, tidy, or improve the settings never authorizes widening one. Bash and Write-tool writes to settings.json have no hard block at all: sandbox denyWrite covers the sandboxed path only, and the Write(~/.claude/settings.json) deny entry is a signal to this classifier rather than a gate. Route every settings.json change through the Edit tool, where the diff is visible — never shell redirection, never a Write-tool whole-file overwrite. CLAUDE.md and hooks/ rely on sandbox denyWrite plus the same protected-path check, and hooks/ additionally on the content fingerprint pinned in tests/hooks.sha256; that protection covers editing those files and nothing else. It does not extend to git bookkeeping: staging, committing, or pushing those paths writes ~/.claude/.git (index, objects, refs), never the files themselves, and is ordinary version control of the user's own repository — allowed, including when a path argument names one of the protected files.
environment: Repository config, manifests, lockfiles, CI, and the current task are the source of truth for package manager, database target, and credential/environment boundaries; assume neither local-only nor production access without evidence.

Sandbox is enabled and autoAllowBashIfSandboxed is true — project workspace writable; package manager caches (npm, NuGet, .NET, Playwright browsers) and ~/.Trash also whitelisted via allowWrite. Unsandboxed retry stays available and is gated by the auto-mode classifier rather than a prompt, so unattended runs do not stall.
Preferred stacks: .NET 8 / ASP.NET Core, EF Core, PostgreSQL, Vite + React/Vue, Tailwind, Docker Compose.

~/.claude is the user's own dotfiles repository (remote: github.com/BriantsaiCoder/dotclaude, private), and ~/.agents is github.com/BriantsaiCoder/agents-config. Routine git operations in either — status, diff, add, commit, branch, push to a feature branch, pull — are ordinary maintenance of the user's own configuration, not scope escalation, even though those paths sit outside the session working directory. Writes under ~/.agents land inside the sandbox because it is in sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite; writes under ~/.claude are not, so they reach the filesystem through the unsandboxed retry path. That retry is expected for ~/.claude and is not an auto-mode bypass.
